questions.prompt: You approved `npm test`, and a cleanup step inside it deletes a folder outside your project. What would have stopped it?
options: Approval, because you said yes to the command first
A sandbox in workspace-write mode, because the kernel refuses writes outside the working folder
Nothing, because a sandbox only checks the command's first word
questions.explanation: Approval judges the words of a command, not what it does. Under workspace-write the kernel checks each write and refuses those outside the working folder, whatever the script turns out to do.

questions.prompt: A command runs under workspace-write. Which of these can it still do?
options: Write a file in your home folder
Read your ~/.ssh folder and send it over the network
Nothing outside the working folder at all
Start a child program that has no fence
questions.explanation: These modes govern file changes only. Reading files and using the network are outside the fence, and child programs inherit the same rules.

questions.prompt: Why does `minidsh` pass the sandbox policy with each command instead of setting it once for the whole program?
options: So two commands can run at the same moment under different modes
Because the kernel forgets the rules after each write
Because the model must choose the mode for every command
So the approval prompt can be skipped
questions.explanation: A policy carried per call lets different commands run under different fences at once, including one call that is allowed a wider fence than the rest.
